answer.evidence: The sloped roof of laid-flat doors fills rows 1-28. It widens from 50 to 62 px going down and is split into two courses by a dark shadow band at rows 15-16. A tan front-edge line at row 29 follows, then dark eave shadow at rows 30-33. Below that is a vertical front wall of stacked pallets, rows 34-62. It has a plank lintel at rows 34-35 and a dark entrance opening with a sack inside. The roof is a clear top plane over a front face of 29 rows, so this is a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 14 visible tones per tile, against 12 and 10 for the references. Near-flat coverage is 5%, so there are no large flat areas. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown, in the tone of the adjacent wood and door frames, rather than being a black sticker line. The pallet wall has slat gaps, a lintel and a dark entrance with a shaded sack. The four door-panel roof sections each carry panel borders, handle details and a few tone steps. The ramps are slightly shallower than the references' 5-6 step tile and plaster ramps, and the roof panels are a little less grainy. Overall it is a dense, correctly structured building of the right kind, and a careful artist would accept it next to the references. It is smaller and simpler, but not flatter.
